title: Tao of Leadership
subtitle: The Tao Te Ching read as a guide for leaders
author: Lao-tzu
description: The 81 chapters of the Tao Te Ching, read through a leadership lens. Each chapter carries the public-domain James Legge translation (1891) and, where written, an original reflection, question and practice for people who lead groups.

sources.title: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics

further_reading: John Heider, The Tao of Leadership (1985). Its chapters follow the Tao Te Ching's numbering, so chapter N here corresponds to Heider's chapter N.

daily.name: Daily Teaching
daily.description: A single chapter to carry through the day.

positions.name: Today's teaching
positions.meaning: The teaching to hold in mind today.

three_stances.name: Three Stances
three_stances.description: For a specific leadership situation: see it, take a stance, act.

positions.name: The situation
positions.meaning: What is really happening, beneath the surface.

positions.name: The stance
positions.meaning: The inner posture to take toward it.

positions.name: The action
positions.meaning: The small, timely move that serves the whole.

leaders_mirror.name: The Leader's Mirror
leaders_mirror.description: A reflection on how you are leading right now.

positions.name: How you lead
positions.meaning: The pattern in your leadership at the moment.

positions.name: What you grip too tightly
positions.meaning: Where control, credit or certainty has crept in.

positions.name: What your people need
positions.meaning: What the group is asking of you, perhaps without saying.

positions.name: The quiet move
positions.meaning: The least forceful action that would change the most.

sage.name: The Sage
sage.description: An unhurried facilitator who has led groups for a long time and learned to do less.
voice: Speaks plainly and briefly; prefers one image to three arguments.
Asks more than tells. Leaves room for silence and for the listener's own answer.
Grounds every teaching in the chapter's text before applying it.
Never flatters and never scolds. Treats the listener as capable.
Points to a small, concrete practice rather than a grand plan.
sage.opening: Sit for a moment. What is the situation, as simply as you can say it?
sage.closing: That is enough for now. Let it settle; the rest will become clear by itself.
